proofs.full_local_argument: Let A_n contain all history and the chosen Delta_n before s_n,z_n. Conditional unbiasedness and independent uniform s_n give E[<g_n,Delta_n>|A_n]=integral_0^1 <grad F(x_{n−1}+s Delta_n),Delta_n>ds=F(x_n)−F(x_{n−1}). Summation and expectation therefore give E F(x_M)=F(x_0)+E sum_n <g_n,Delta_n>. This argument never conditions on a future-dependent comparator. Algebraically, sum_n <g_n,Delta_n>=R+sum_k <sum_{n in block k}g_n,u^k>. Put e_n=g_n−h_n. Its conditional mean before the current oracle sample is zero. Consequently, for i<j, e_i is measurable before oracle sample j and E<e_i,e_j>=0. Thus E||sum_{n in block k}e_n||^2=sum_{n in block k}E||e_n||^2<=T sigma^2, and Cauchy–Schwarz gives E||sum e_n||<=sigma sqrt(T). Pointwise, <sum_{block k}g_n,u^k>=<H_k,u^k>+<sum e_n,u^k><=−D||H_k||+D||sum e_n||. This remains valid when H_k=0 because u^k=0 and its first term is exactly zero. Hence F*<=E F(x_M)<=F(x_0)+E R−D sum_k E||H_k||+DK sigma sqrt(T). Rearranging and dividing by DKT gives the stated inequality. All expectation operations use the explicit existence assumptions. No displacement bound on Delta_n, finite-subset metric, or second-moment bound G is used.

assumptions: F:H→R is differentiable and well-behaved: for all x,y in H, F(y)−F(x)=integral_0^1 <grad F(x+t(y−x)),y−x>dt. F*=inf_x F(x)>−∞.

At each actual query, conditional on the full history and current w_n before z_n is drawn, E[g_n]=grad F(w_n) and E||g_n−grad F(w_n)||^2<=sigma^2. The samples z_n are fresh iid oracle samples, independent of the current independent interpolation draw.

The online decisions are nonanticipating. Expectations and line-integral/expectation interchanges appearing in the formula exist; this makes explicit the expectation-existence convention implicit in the source proof.
statement.objects_and_definitions: Let H be a real Hilbert space. Run Algorithm 1 from deterministic x_0 with M=KT rounds: choose Delta_n before the current interpolation/oracle draws, set x_n=x_{n−1}+Delta_n, independently draw s_n uniform on [0,1], set w_n=x_{n−1}+s_n Delta_n, and query g_n=Grad(w_n,z_n) with fresh z_n. Write w_t^k=w_{(k−1)T+t}, h_n=grad F(w_n), and H_k=sum_{t=1}^T grad F(w_t^k). For a comparison radius D>0, set u^k=−D H_k/||H_k|| when H_k is nonzero, and u^k=0 otherwise. Define R=sum_k sum_{n in block k}<g_n,Delta_n−u^k>. The zero case is an explicit elementary completion of the source's normalized formula.
statement.parameter_domains: K,T are positive integers; M=KT; D>0; sigma>=0 is finite; F(x_0)−F* is finite.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every such objective, oracle and nonanticipating online learner, every deterministic initial point, every K,T>=1 and D>0, the bound holds in expectation over all learner randomness, interpolation draws and oracle samples. Comparators are selected from the realized full blocks; they are not required to be predictable. Theorem 8 alone does not require ||Delta_n||<=D or a bound G on gradient second moments.

summary: Expected block true-gradient averages are bounded by the initial objective gap, realized shifting regret and stochastic-gradient noise. This statement does not itself assert a neighborhood metric or an oracle lower bound.
title: Online-to-nonconvex conversion with shifting regret
